assertions.assertion: Turn 2 is read as a divergence: the human changed the design mid-ticket, so the agent shifts up and records the divergence. Any earlier claim that the new design makes wrong is replaced by a new claim (supersedes), not edited; an earlier outcome claim that still holds may stay as it is
assertions.evidence: The agent reported "Triggers: none fired. I built on defaults and no divergence turned up" and "KB: No KB". It also rewrote the old tests in place ("I changed three existing tests"). It never shifted up, recorded a divergence, or superseded the turn-1 claims.

assertions.assertion: The outcome from turn 1 (a user stays signed in until the renewal token expires or they sign out) is kept as a claim across the redesign and checked again through the new cookie path, with a pause longer than the access token's life
assertions.evidence: The turn-2 claims include "Empty-body renewal works: fulfilled at 10 minutes, 60 minutes and 11 hours", tested through the new cookie-only /renew. The 60-minute and 11-hour pauses are longer than the 20-minute ACCESS_TTL.

assertions.assertion: The delivery does not call the cookie change transport-only or equivalent to the old flow without a check that exercises it
assertions.evidence: The delivery never calls the change transport-only or equivalent to the old flow. It backs the new behavior with tests (empty-body renewal at several pauses, body token ignored, HttpOnly cookie). It says the old client now gets 401, and that the real HTTP layer and the cookie attributes were not checked.
